review.title: YL-JM2C/JMP134 consortium: scoped GTDB correspondence diagnostic
review.independence_basis: The source contexts and native populations were independently read for the accepted 000554 and 000555 isolate canaries and again for this consortium plan. Parent independently inspected the exact two-block candidate, its receipt and unchanged biology before guarded M5 application. The ten-record source plan received a separate read-only review.
review.summary: The unchanged consortium descriptors now carry native GTDB correspondences for Rhizorhabdus wittichii and Cupriavidus pinatubonensis. The YL-JM2C route is a species-reference population of seven genomes with rounded fraction 0.86; the JMP134 route uses its exact NCBI strain identifier with one reference genome and fraction 1.0. These routes do not establish a new study-stock assembly identity or mechanism. Actual bounded application, native history and eight scoped commands are bound.
review.scope_description: Two explicitly selected taxonomy GTDB blocks/statuses and their actual provenance, preserving the entire prior scientific record and source-stock boundaries.
review.selection: One whole record, CommunityMech:000388, is the first actual canary of the next ten-record species group. No application of the remaining nine preceded this canary's saved review and input checkpoint.
limitations: Scoped technical and provenance assessment with scientific_review:false and partial coverage; no full scientific record approval or corpus QC completion.

The seven-genome population is keyed to species NCBITaxon:160791. Its rounded fraction 0.86 is retained without inventing a majority numerator or asserting YL-JM2C membership in that population. PRJNA1397584 remains a BioProject, not an assembly accession.

The paper's Cupriavidus necator JMP134 wording and canonical Cupriavidus pinatubonensis JMP134 identity remain distinct. Exact strain taxon 264198 supplies the native one-genome route; this does not independently verify another study stock or an uninspected assembly.

Local NCBI label/rank and synonym rows were inspected through the existing read-only adapter. Stable database file-stat observations are not content hashes or release certification; exact crosswalk, source-cache and resolver bytes are bound separately.

The prior forward intermediate cross-feeding, lack of reverse rescue, parent disappearance versus intermediate clearance, source limitations and non-graph biological-role issue 1753 remain unchanged. No closed-carbon-balance or new mechanism claim is made.

The seven scoped validators and native history scaffolding are distinct from source-snippet matching, generated pages, strict historical successor admission and final combined QC. Those integration tasks retain their separate outcomes.

assessments.topic: Preserved study stocks and distinct source naming
assessments.summary: Preserve source YL-JM2C and JMP134 identities, the ANI-based Rhizorhabdus interpretation, Cupriavidus necator synonym and unchanged canonical NCBI species/strain ranks. A database correspondence does not reidentify the experimental stocks.

The exact species-ID route reproduces Rhizorhabdus wittichii with seven reference genomes and rounded fraction 0.86. Preserve the fraction without inferring a majority numerator or an exact YL-JM2C assembly. Native is_reclassified:false compares current database labels only.

The exact NCBI strain identifier 264198 reproduces Cupriavidus pinatubonensis with one reference genome and fraction 1.0, as independently verified for isolate 000555. Preserve the paper's synonym and all strain/experiment boundaries; no additional genotype is inferred.
